idiom_name: ButtonGroup owns the exclusive selection; children join it with add()/setGroup()
implementation_notes: The JDK already ships the group object the pattern needs: a ButtonGroup owns the exclusive selection, and children declare membership with add() or setGroup(), after which the group clears the previously selected button itself - the parent reads the model once (getSelection) instead of walking children. What replaces the classic structure is that toolkit primitive; hand-written parent state is justified only for invariants the toolkit does not model, such as validation spanning several independent fields. Note that a ButtonGroup is not a Container - it carries no layout or rendering responsibility - so the composition stays with the ordinary container hierarchy, and the group only holds the selection model.
pitfalls: Forgetting to add a button to both the container and the group yields a visible but ungrouped option that can stay selected twice.
Removing a button from a group does not clear its selected state - update the model explicitly when children are rebuilt.
Per-button listeners multiply; prefer one shared Action or a group-level listener so behaviour stays in the parent.
ButtonGroup is not serializable and not a component - don't expect it to appear in the container hierarchy or persist itself.

variants.name: JavaFX ToggleGroup for ToggleButton/RadioButton children
variants.implementation_notes: JavaFX's ToggleGroup plays the same role for ToggleButton and RadioButton children and adds the observable model the pattern wants: selectedToggleProperty can be bound or listened to, and setUserData attaches the domain value to each child so the parent maps a selection to data in one place. Membership goes through setToggleGroup (or by declaring the group in FXML), and exclusivity is automatic - choose this variant where the UI is JavaFX rather than Swing. The module no longer ships with the JDK, so the OpenJFX dependency and its module path become part of the pattern's preconditions.
variants.idiom_name: ToggleGroup owns exclusivity; selectedToggleProperty is the parent's observable model
pitfalls: A ToggleButton in a ToggleGroup cannot be deselected by clicking again - model an optional selection with an extra 'none' toggle or allow user-deselect semantics.
selectedToggle can become null (all children deselected), so listeners must handle a null new value instead of casting blindly.
JavaFX ships separately from the JDK since 11; an unconfigured module path fails at startup, not at compile time.
